title: When the Orbit Breaks Again
premise: Lior Sandoval, a terraformer hauling cargo through the contested orbits of Kepler Station, intercepts a distress signal in a language extinct since the Veyan Massacre two centuries ago. The signal leads her to a derelict seed-vault ship whose black-box archives prove the massacre was ordered by the founding families who now rule the colonies—and whose descendants have spent generations rewriting every record. As Earth's final transmission loop counts down to permanent silence, Lior must smuggle the archive past corporate enforcers and her own complicit past, broadcasting the truth before the last window closes. She succeeds at devastating cost: her garden, her crew, and her anonymity are destroyed, but the truth takes root among a generation that finally learns what it inherited.
about_author: M. M. Delacroix is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals for deep-space cargo contracts before turning to fiction. They live somewhere with too much rain and write about gardens that refuse to die.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Establishes her routine hauling terraforming cargo through contested orbits and tending the generational garden aboard Kepler Station—a project for colonists not yet born. She values invisibility above all. Emotional beat: weary contentment masking old guilt over something she abandoned years ago.

chapters.title: The Signal That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A distress ping arrives in Old Veyan, a language extinct since the massacre. Her ship's translator fails; only her grandmother's lullabies let her parse fragments. Emotional beat: dread and reluctant recognition—she is one of perhaps a dozen living speakers.

chapters.title: Cargo Manifests and Ghost Ships
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Lior and station archivist Tomas Reyes. They trace the signal to coordinates inside a restricted shipping lane owned by Halcyon Combine. Tomas warns that querying those records flags them. Emotional beat: the first crack in Lior's invisibility; curiosity outweighing fear.

chapters.title: The Seed-Vault Meridian
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She finds the derelict vault ship Meridian, hull breached but life-support flickering, filled with frozen embryos and sealed data cores. A dying maintenance AI addresses her in Veyan. Emotional beat: awe curdling into horror as she realizes the ship was meant to be found by no one.

chapters.title: What the Black Box Remembers
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Decrypted logs show colony defense fleets firing on unarmed Veyan transports—and orders signed by Aldous Wren, patriarch of the family that now governs the colonies. Every public record names the Veyans as aggressors. Emotional beat: vertigo of discovering history itself was manufactured.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Lies
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, interwoven with childhood flashbacks. She recalls her grandmother's whispered stories dismissed as trauma-fictions, and understands why her family hid their language. Emotional beat: grief reframed—the shame she carried was engineered.

chapters.title: The Loop
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Earth's last transmission loop, a century-old broadcast relay, will end in forty days when its power core is decommissioned. After that, no independent channel exists to reach the inner colonies. Emotional beat: a ticking clock made physical; hope requires an impossible deadline.

chapters.title: Halcyon Comes Knocking
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Combine auditors board Kepler Station asking about anomalous signals. Lior lies smoothly and hates how good she's become at it. Her crewmate Dev notices. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening; survival instinct versus the growing need to act.

chapters.title: Dev
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. He confronts Lior, revealing he lost family on a Veyan-listed transport and has spent years believing they were terrorists. Lior shows him one decrypted log entry. Emotional beat: shattered faith, then fierce alliance—he joins her not from proof but from need.

chapters.title: The Archive Run
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A tense salvage run extracts the Meridian's core while dodging Combine patrol drones. The AI sacrifices its remaining power to mask their approach. Emotional beat: adrenaline and mourning—the last voice of old Veya goes silent helping her.

chapters.title: Price of Passage
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. To move the core off-station, they bribe a dockmaster with Tomas's irreplaceable archival access—burning his career and safety. Emotional beat: the theme crystallizes; every step toward truth costs something irreplaceable.

chapters.title: Wren Descendant
chapters.summary: New POV: Ilsa Wren, young heir to the Combine, discovers her family's private vault contains the original massacre orders. Raised on the official story, she begins quietly verifying. Emotional beat: inheritance as poison; loyalty to blood versus loyalty to truth.

chapters.title: Two Kinds of Proof
chapters.summary: Lior and Ilsa's paths nearly cross at a Combine gala where Lior infiltrates as cargo staff. Ilsa notices a woman humming a Veyan lullaby. Emotional beat: electric near-miss; both women realize the other exists.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Cold
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Under interrogation after a routine stop, Dev gives up partial information—not the core's location, but enough that Combine hunters now know someone aboard Kepler has it. Emotional beat: guilt without betrayal; he protected Lior at the cost of the mission's cover.

chapters.title: Siege of Kepler Station
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Combine forces quarantine the station, searching ship by ship. Lior hides the core inside the generational garden's nutrient systems—the one place auditors won't contaminate. Emotional beat: the garden becomes sanctuary; what she grew for the future now guards the past.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Choice
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She confirms the massacre orders, confronts her father, and is disowned and confined. Using her access codes one last time, she transmits a warning to Lior: the loop's shutdown has been moved up nine days. Emotional beat: an heir burning her inheritance to hand the match to a stranger.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Escape plan: ride a routine terraformer supply barge to the loop relay, disguised as fertilizer shipment. Dev insists on piloting the decoy run. Emotional beat: grim resolve; the plan works only if everyone accepts they might not come back.

chapters.title: The Breaking Orbit
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The decoy is intercepted; Dev's ship is destroyed buying time, and Lior watches from the barge, unable to turn back. Emotional beat: the price of survival made flesh—she lives because he didn't, and must carry it.

chapters.title: Last Transmission
chapters.summary: Climax, Lior's POV. At the relay, Combine troops close in as Lior splices the archive into the dying loop. Ilsa's stolen codes hold the door for ninety seconds. The full massacre record broadcasts across every colony channel as the core dies forever. Emotional beat: triumph inseparable from loss; the truth escapes exactly once.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Multi-POV epilogue-style chapter. Colonies erupt; Wren loyalists fall; Ilsa testifies against her own name. Lior, exposed and hunted no longer but never safe again, returns to a ransacked station. Emotional beat: hollow victory—the world changed, her old life unrecoverable.

chapters.title: What Grows in Broken Ground
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Months later, the garden survives, and new settlers—many of Veyan descent—ask her to teach the language. She plants the Meridian's recovered seed stock in open ground for the first time. Emotional beat: quiet renewal; inheritance reclaimed as gift rather than burden.

chapters.title: When the Orbit Breaks Again
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Lior's POV. Another faint signal arrives—older, farther, in yet another silenced tongue. This time, dozens answer the call alongside her. Lior smiles, loads the cargo, and burns for the dark. Emotional beat: cyclical hope; survival's price paid forward into vigilance.
